reviews.review: One of the best game ever!

Pros:
Basic combat
Gore
Guns
Art
Chainsword
Jetpack segments

Cons:
Level design
Setpieces
Not enough variety in the combat
Needs more bosses
Quick time events
Much shorter than I though
Crap multiplayer
Camera

Overall:
Mediocre

So I bought this off of the back of Totalbiscuit's nerdgasm of a First Impressions video. Unfortunately, for whatever reason, I encounted unbearable reverb on the sound effects that drowned out music and dialogue. Worse, even Space Marine's pretty dedicated fanbase is apparently unable to fix. But I muted the soundeffects (music & voice acting is fine) and proceeded onwards.  The gameplay is good, nice weapon and enemy variety, voice acting is pretty solid and the story is passable enough. I haven't touched the multiplayer.

Then, my save file corrupted and I ended up stuck at the end of a level with an absent cutscene trigger. It has a single savefile (smauto.dsav) hidden away in the Steam userdata folder, which you can only back up by copying and pasting.

Sega Support's only solution was create a new save file AKA restart the campaign. Let's just say I wasn't happy.

Though I liked playing it, I'm can't recommend it. The lack of soundeffects soured the experience considerably, let alone the eleven hours of gameplay lost to a in-game save system that is frankly unfit for PC. I shouldn't have to exit the game to create a separate save file. These two issues have killed any desire I had to play the game.

It is however a rarely authentic Warhammer 40k experience. If you buy it, remember to back up your saves regularly to save yourself some grief.

[b]TL;DR[/b]
+Positives+
[list]
[*]Authentic Warhammer 40k
[*]Good gunplay, simple yet fun melee
[*]Varied enemies & weapons
[*]Solid performance by the cast
[/list]

-Negatives-
[list]
[*]An unfixable bug that creates unbearable reverb on sound effects.
[*]Muted weapons make me sad.
[*]Single save file system is susceptible to corruption, which will force you to restart the campaign.
[*]Manually saving (as in locate, copy and paste the smauto.dsav) is annoying.
[/list]

A solid game with one immersion-killing technical issue and another of the potentially gamebreaking variety. Your experiences may differ, but it might not.
